title: Alignment Garden — plan & exec notes v0.1
summary: Working draft for a lightweight, repeatable cadence we can use for quarterly alignment. Mix of OKR candidates, exec update notes, and an abbreviated all-hands run-of-show. Treat as scratchpad — marked open questions and clear owner callouts.
body:
Context
- Motivation: our current quarterly handoff feels heavy and brittle. Several teams reported duplicated asks, misaligned rollouts, and unclear escalation paths during the last quarter. This doc sketches a simplified cadence (the "Alignment Garden") we can pilot for the next quarter.
- Goal: reduce cross-org friction on priorities while keeping the exec and all-hands cadence compact (<= 90 minutes total planning time per quarter for exec + all-hands prep).

High-level approach (garden metaphor)
- Plot: shared company priorities (3 top objectives) planted centrally.
- Beds: team-level commitments that feed into each objective; short notes visible to all.
- Weeds: open risks and blockers tracked in a shared triage list and cleaned weekly.

Proposed Company Objectives (draft OKRs)
1) Objective A — Make inference predictable and cheaper for customers
   - KR A1: Reduce median token cost by 18% on hosted API for top 10 customers (owner: Evan Carter)
   - KR A2: 99.9% success rate on production inference for 95th pct latency windows for Dedicated (owner: infra-sre rotation)
   - KR A3: Document and publish 3 model-quantization profiles for high-throughput workloads (owner: Applied ML)

2) Objective B — Expand enterprise-ready private deployments
   - KR B1: Close 2 pilot customers on Private with on-prem install and SOC2 control checklist satisfied (owner: Priya Nair)
   - KR B2: Private onboarding automation reduces average spin-up time from 6 weeks to 3 weeks (owner: solutions-eng)

3) Objective C — Developer experience & observability
   - KR C1: 80% of new customers complete our quickstart and run a sample inference within 24 hours (owner: devexp)
   - KR C2: Ship token-level cost UI and route-level latency breakdown in Console (owner: product-console)

Notes on framing: these are intentionally conservative KRs to prioritize reliability and reduce risk. We can expand stretch targets after pilot quarter.

All-hands & Exec prep (compact runbook)
- Timeline:
  - Week -4: Draft OKRs circulated to exec and product leads (owner: Rebecca Lin)
  - Week -3: Feedback cycle; two synchronous office hours for feedback (owner: Maya Zhou)
  - Week -2: Finalize slides and shared one-pager (owner: comms + product ops)
  - Week -1: Dry run exec update (30m), finalize run-of-show for company (owner: exec-assist)
  - D-day: All-hands (60 minutes) + department breakouts (30 minutes optional)
- Run-of-show (60 min):
  - 0–5m: Welcome + 1 slide top-line (CEO)
  - 5–20m: State of the product — 3 objectives + 1 highlight per objective (product lead)
  - 20–35m: Customer signal & revenue context (GTM lead)
  - 35–45m: Ops reliability update + comms on Dedicated/Private progress (SRE/infra lead)
  - 45–55m: Team highlights (3 teams, 3 slides each)
  - 55–60m: Asks, next steps, and where to find the details (Rebecca)

Open questions / decisions required
- Q1: How many OKRs should be company-level vs. program-level? Recommendation: cap company-level at 3 objectives.
- Q2: SLA story for Dedicated — are we ready to publish a public latency SLA or keep it private for customers? Need legal + infra input (owner: Tomás).
- Q3: All-hands length — do we keep to 60 minutes or expand for more demos? Exec preference: keep concise.

Operational cadence & tooling
- We propose a lightweight shared spreadsheet for the pilot (sheet links in linked_artifacts). Columns: objective, KR, owner, status (R/A/G), quarter progress notes, blockers.
- Weekly 15m cross-org triage meeting (exec+ops reps) to remove weeds.
- Runbook updates: store the final run-of-show and slide deck in Confluence under /company/alignment-garden.

Risks / "weeds"
- Risk: Too many program-level goals diluting focus. Mitigation: stage 2 review to prune non-core KRs (owner: Rebecca).
- Risk: Customer pilots for Private take longer than expected. Mitigation: prioritize two pilot customers with clear acceptance criteria; spin up a small escrowed infra team for each pilot (owner: Priya).
- Risk: Communication fatigue across teams leading to missed feedback. Mitigation: two-tier feedback windows (asynchronous comments + two live office hours).

Action items (first 30 days)
- A1: Share this draft with exec and product leads for prioritization (owner: Rebecca) — due 2026-03-10
- A2: Construct the shared OKR sheet and seed with team inputs (owner: Maya) — due 2026-03-15
- A3: Book office hours and invite all team leads (owner: comms) — due 2026-03-12
- A4: Prepare a stripped-down all-hands slide deck (10 slides max) for dry run (owner: product ops) — due 2026-03-22

Working notes / scratchpad
- Things to consider: compressing the ops update into one slide (key metrics only), focusing demos on customer ROI, and surfacing any model-quality regressions tied to deployments.
- Slack threads to reference: #product-roadmap (thread pinned: "alignment-garden-okr-feedback"), #infra-ops (ticket JIRA-OPS-789).

Appendix: quick references
- Draft OKR sheet: JIRA-OPS-789 attached (see linked artifacts)
- Prior all-hands artifacts: archived in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts)

Notes to self: this language should stay informal for now — we want people to edit in place. After the pilot quarter, move to a formal playbook and add templates for the deck and OKR sheet.
